tasks.task_text: Identify the areas covered by exactly one of two polygon layers (an exterior-extent layer and a survey layer) — regions present in one layer but not in both. Output: a polygon layer of the non-overlapping areas. Any valid route to this result is acceptable.

Generate a polygon layer of uniform-width bands tracing the boundaries of input polygons, for tactile-map edge rendering. The band width is user-specified and bands must be centred on the original outlines, free of geometry artefacts, and combined into a clean output. Output: polygon features representing the edge bands.

From a high-resolution DEM, produce three terrain-derivative rasters: slope in degrees, aspect in degrees, and a hillshade. The derivatives must be geometrically meaningful, which requires working in a projected metric CRS. Output: three georeferenced raster files added to the project.

Produce a per-municipality dominant drought-class map from a drought-severity polygon layer whose classes overlap. Overlaps must be resolved so that more severe classes take precedence (hierarchical exclusivity). For each municipality, determine the drought class covering the largest area within it. Output: (1) a municipality layer symbolized by dominant drought class and (2) a table listing each municipality's dominant class code/name and the corresponding area.

From a vector layer, select the features whose string attribute matches a given case-insensitive pattern. Report (a) the total number of input features and (b) the number of matching features, and produce (c) the centroid of the matching features' merged geometry as a single point. Output: the matching features carrying both counts, and one centroid point feature carrying the same counts.

Map seafloor substrate units from ROV navigation tracks and annotations: for each annotated location, represent the area of seafloor visible to the camera as a substrate-classified polygon oriented along the track, then combine overlapping areas so each final unit carries a single substrate class. Output: a polygon layer of substrate mapping units with standardized styling.

Merge small forest-stand polygons into adjacent, similar, larger stands. A small stand is eligible only when it touches a larger neighbour, the relative difference in dominant height stays within the given threshold, and the neighbour is of a qualifying type ('classified'). Each merged group must retain the attributes of its largest stand, and each output feature must state whether it was merged (merged = 1) or not (merged = 0). Output: a merged polygon layer.

Compute per-country mean values of several raster indicators using country boundaries as zones: land quality (one epoch) and population density for the years 1500, 1990, and 2000. Retain the country name and ISO code fields, attach one distinctly prefixed set of statistics per indicator epoch, and export the final attribute table as CSV. Output: a countries layer carrying all statistics, plus the exported CSV file.

Draw a representative sample of points from an input point layer based on the values of a numeric attribute. The sampling must support both a simple random mode and a stratified mode, in which the numeric field is first divided into classes (e.g., by quantiles or equal intervals) and points are sampled within each class. Output: a new point layer containing the sampled features with X and Y coordinate fields added.

Combine two polygon zoning layers (e.g., management zones and soil zones) into a single layer of non-overlapping atomic zones, where each output polygon represents a unique combination of the two zonings. The output must consist of valid single-part polygons, each uniquely identified. Output: one polygon layer with a unique zone ID and geometry attributes (area, perimeter) per zone.

For a water-network vector layer restricted to a study area, produce results organized by the network's three hierarchical levels (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria) according to the level attribute: one layer per level and a buffer zone around each level with its own specified radius (each level has a distinct radius). Output: the study-area network, one filtered layer per level, and one buffer layer per level.

For each paddock polygon, produce a distance raster giving, for every location inside the paddock, the distance to the nearest water point located within that same paddock, in map units of the working CRS. Paddocks containing at least one water point each yield their own georeferenced distance raster named after the paddock; the set of per-paddock rasters is the final output — no additional summary statistic is required.

Assemble a natural-resource dataset for a specified property: obtain the relevant natural-resource features from the government feature service for the given lot/plan boundaries or extent, so that the final dataset covers exactly the target property area. Output: a single styled GeoPackage layer containing the property's natural-resource data.

For each polygon in an input layer, compute the area-weighted average of a numeric attribute from an overlay polygon layer, ensuring duplicated overlay geometry is not counted twice. Output: the input features with the area-weighted average attached, plus a report layer with per-feature details; a CRS check is expected for geographic or mismatched layers.

Estimate noise levels (dBA) at receptor locations around a point noise source according to the BS 5228 standard, accounting for terrain between source and receptors, distance attenuation, ground type, and barriers. Input: a point source, receptor polygons, and a DEM; layers must be handled in a projected CRS. Output: a noise-level value per receptor and a styled source-point layer.

For each species-occurrence point, summarise a continuous environmental raster within a circular neighbourhood of a user-specified radius: compute the requested statistics of the raster inside each neighbourhood and attach them to the original point locations. Output: the occurrence points enriched with the neighbourhood statistics.

Select valid canopy-photo locations from a set of candidate points, an optimized flight grid, and an area plot polygon. The selected locations must satisfy the specified spatial safety constraints and use the required projected coordinate reference system. Output: a 'Safe Points' layer of locations valid for canopy photo capture.

Within a user-defined area of interest, assign a Manning roughness coefficient to CORINE 2018 land-cover polygons, using the provided CODE_18→n lookup table, and compute each polygon's area in square metres and hectares. All outputs must be in a common CRS. Output: the AOI land-cover polygons with Manning and area attributes, loaded for visualization.

Align multiple input rasters to a common grid — identical CRS, extent, and pixel size — so they can be stacked for a multi-criteria suitability analysis. Alignment must honour a reference (snap) grid where provided. Output: a set of aligned rasters with identical grid structure, plus a manifest summarizing the alignment parameters used.

Task: Identify floating ice lid
Identify floating ice lid areas in a lake region by analyzing SAR backscatter intensity and optical-derived dark shadow features from Landsat 8, using thresholding on normalized HH band values and masking with optical data to classify frozen, undecided, and floating ice zones.

Task: Classify coral and sand habitats
Classify benthic habitats (coral, sand, and deep water) in the Belitung region using Lyzenga's water column correction applied to Landsat 8 surface reflectance data, followed by Random Forest and SVM classification on B2_median band, with accuracy assessment from training data.

Task: Calculate sagebrush ecosystem integrity
Calculate the Sagebrush Ecosystem Integrity (SEI) index using simulated aboveground biomass outputs from STEPWAT — specifically sagebrush, perennial forbs/grasses, and annual forbs/grasses — converted to ecological quality (Q) scores via ecoregion-specific cover-biomass relationships (q-curves). It combines these Q scores multiplicatively with existing threat layers (tree encroachment, human modification) to produce a continuous SEI560 metric, then applies Gaussian smoothing at 2000 m radius (SEI2000), classifies the result into deciles, and reclassifies into three management classes: 'core', 'grow', and 'treat'. Outputs are multi-band Earth Engine image assets containing raw Q layers, SEI560, SEI2000, decile-classified SEI, and 3-class management designations for current and future climate scenarios (RCP45, 2070–2100).

Task: Extract monthly surface pressure
Extract monthly mean surface pressure from ERA5 reanalysis data for the period 2000–2020 at specific ASOS station locations, computes the average value across 20 years for each month, and exports the results per station.

Task: Model bear habitat suitability
the workflow models habitat suitability for bears using presence points and environmental predictors, generating a probability map of suitable habitat and a binary potential distribution map. It employs spatial block cross-validation with random forests to train and validate the model, then averages predictions across iterations to produce a final habitat suitability map. Outputs include variable importance, training/testing partitions, and an estimated area of potential distribution in square kilometers.

Task: Estimate forest cover from fractional vegetation
Estimate forest area and percentage cover in Nicaragua for March 2020 using MODIS MCD43A4 surface reflectance data. It applies a spectral mixture analysis (SMA) to derive bare soil, photosynthetic vegetation (PV), and non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV) fractions, then classifies canopy cover where PV > 0.6 and bare < 0.4. Results include printed statistics for estimated forest area in square kilometers and percent forest cover, along with time-series charting of fractional cover from 2017–2020. The output visualizations include SMA results, forest cover maps, and protected areas overlay.

Task: Model heating and cooling degree days
the workflow models fuzzy heating and cooling degree days using daily minimum and maximum temperature projections from the CESM1-BGC climate model under historical and RCP scenarios (rcp45, rcp85). It calculates daily mean temperatures, applies fuzzy logic thresholds (with and without 3-day averaging) to estimate building energy demand proxies, and exports annual raster maps of heating and cooling days for 2000 (historical) and 2050 (future projection), including their differences. The outputs are masked to land areas using MODIS land cover data and visualized with custom color palettes.

Task: Model permafrost thermal state
the workflow models the spatial distribution of permafrost thermal state (ALT - Active Layer Thickness) using kriging interpolation and Random Forest regression. It first performs geostatistical interpolation (kriging) on ALT point data to generate a continuous surface, then combines it with environmental covariates (e.g., soil properties, climate indices, NDVI, NDSI) to train a machine learning model. The final output is a classified raster map of estimated ALT (E), validated through training accuracy metrics and variable importance charts, with results exported as assets and visualized on the map.

Task: Quantify VIIRS active fire FRP and area
the workflow quantifies monthly VIIRS (VNP14IMGML) active fire radiative power (FRP in MW) and burned area (in km²) at 375 m resolution, disaggregated by spatial overlap with MODIS Aqua FRP, MODIS Terra FRP, and MODIS MCD64A1 burned area within user-selected GFEDv4 basis regions (e.g., Basis 1). It computes four mutually exclusive VIIRS fire metrics: total VIIRS FRP/area (AF), VIIRS FRP/area outside MODIS Aqua FRP (AFnoAqua), outside MODIS burned area (AFnoBA), and outside all MODIS fire observations (AFnoMODIS). These are aggregated via reduceRegions to sum statistics per GFEDv4 polygon and exported as CSV tables containing summed FRP (MW) and area (km²) per 0.25° grid cell (implicitly via polygon-level aggregation over GFED basis region geometry).

Task: Monitor maritime activity intensity
Monitor maritime activity intensity in the Port of Singapore using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery by generating a median VV/VH polarisation composite over 2023, visualising backscatter characteristics for vessel detection and sea surface analysis, and quantifying temporal acquisition density via monthly image counts — outputs include clipped composite rasters (VV/VH), a study area boundary layer, summary statistics (total/ascending/descending image counts), and a monthly column chart of image availability.

Task: Monitor crop health using NDVI time series
Monitor agricultural crop health across Punjab’s agricultural areas using Sentinel-2 Harmonized Surface Reflectance imagery from 2024–2025. It applies cloud masking (via QA60 bit flags), calculates NDVI (B8/B4), EVI, NDRE, and SAVI, generates a monthly NDVI time series chart, produces classified crop health maps (5-tier: Stressed to Very Healthy) based on NDVI thresholds, computes NDVI anomaly for stress detection, exports latest NDVI, mean NDVI, peak NDVI, health classification, and regional NDVI statistics as GeoTIFFs and CSV — all tailored for operational crop stress assessment and seasonal health tracking.

Task: Estimate water depth using SDB
Estimate shallow water bathymetry using the Lyzenga's Simple Depth Band Ratio (SDB) method on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2020 to 2022. It applies cloud masking by joining S2_CLOUD_PROBABILITY with S2_SR, computes log-transformed band ratios for blue, green, and red bands, and performs linear regression using in-situ depth points. The model is trained on 80% of the points and validated on 20%, producing a scatter plot of estimated vs. actual depths with R² and RMSE. The final output is a calibrated bathymetric raster map exported to Earth Engine Assets.

Task: Analyze aerosol reflectance over AOI
Analyze mean aerosol reflectance in the B1 band (ultra-blue) of Sentinel-2 imagery over a small AOI from 2016-09-01 to 2017-09-30. It filters the Sentinel-2 image collection by date and region, clips each image to the AOI, computes the mean value of band B1 using reduceRegion, and appends this statistic as a property ('Aerosol_Mean') to each image. The output includes the size of the filtered collection, metadata of individual images, and visualization of up to 12 images using a false-color composite (B8, B3, B4), enabling visual inspection of surface and atmospheric features.

Task: Calculate sagebrush ecosystem integrity
Calculate future Sagebrush Ecosystem Integrity (SEI) using Method 1 from Doherty et al. 2022: it computes scaled percent change in STEPWAT-simulated biomass (sage, perennial grass, annual forb/grass) under climate scenarios (RCP45, 2070–2100), multiplies these delta-S values by current smoothed percent cover layers (sage560m, perennialG560m, annualG560m) from RAP (Rangeland Analysis Platform), converts to Habitat Suitability Index (HSI) using ecoregion-specific curves (Great Basin, Intermountain, Plains), integrates resources and threats multiplicatively (Q1–Q5) to produce continuous SEI560, applies Gaussian smoothing at 2000 m radius to yield SEI2000, classifies into deciles, then reclassifies into three management classes (core/grow/treat), and exports a multi-band GEE Image Asset containing all intermediate and final layers (Q1raw–Q5sc3) per GCM.

Task: Analyze groundwater storage time series
Extract and analyzes monthly groundwater storage (GWS) time series from the NASA GLDAS CLSM model over a defined polygonal region in Iran (approximately spanning longitudes 43.67–63.09°E and latitudes 24.94–39.79°N) for the period 2003–2024. It computes monthly mean GWS_tavg values, generates two charts — one showing spatially averaged (over the polygon) monthly GWS evolution, and another showing point-based time series at two user-defined locations (loc1 and loc2) — and exports the full monthly stack as a clipped, multi-band GeoTIFF to Google Drive. The workflow includes date sequence generation, image collection filtering and reduction, metadata annotation (system:time_start/end/index), null-band filtering, and visualization/export setup.

Task: Classify benthic habitats using Random Forest
the workflow performs atmospheric correction using Dark Object Subtraction (DOS) on a satellite image over Misool, then applies a Random Forest classifier to classify benthic habitats into four classes (e.g., water, vegetation, sand, coral) using deglinted bands and a derived index (DII23), based on training samples from ROI_Sunglint. The output is a classified benthic map exported to Google Drive.

Task: Assess drought severity using VHI
Compute the Vegetation Health Index (VHI) over the Irrawaddy Basin using Landsat 7 surface temperature and NDVI data from 2013 to 2020. It derives VHI by combining the Temperature Condition Index (TCI) and Vegetation Condition Index (VCI) during the hot season (March–May) each year, masks areas with NDVI > 0.2 to focus on vegetated regions, and identifies drought-affected areas where VHI < 20. The outputs include annual VHI raster maps exported to Google Drive and CSV files summarizing the total drought-affected area in square kilometers for each year.

Task: Classify ice and water types
Classify pixel-level surface types in lakes into four categories: water, clear ice, opaque ice, and snow using Landsat TOA reflectance data. It trains a Random Forest model on labeled training samples with spectral predictors and validates it temporally by splitting data by year (before/after 2019), ultimately producing a trained classification model for cryospheric surface mapping.

Task: Detect active fires with GOES-17
Process GOES-17 ABI Level 2 Multichannel Cloud and Moisture Imagery (MCMIPF) data to generate true-color and false-color visualizations by applying scale/offset corrections, adding a synthetic green band via spectral blending, and scaling for visualization. It then integrates Fire Detection and Characterization (FDCF) data by mapping confidence values to fire mask codes, filtering for high-confidence fire pixels (≥0.3), and overlaying them on the MCMIPF imagery. The output is a time-lapse visualization collection where active fires are highlighted in red over corrected multispectral imagery, enabling spatiotemporal monitoring of wildfires.

Task: Extract daily height data
Process the RTMA (Real-Time Mesoscale Analysis) dataset to extract daily mean values of the 'HGT' (height) variable from January 1, 2020, to January 31, 2020. It creates an ImageCollection where each image represents the mean height for a single day, renamed by date, and includes time metadata. The output is a time-series collection of daily height fields over North America at high spatial resolution.

Estimate the residential population of individual buildings by combining building-footprint vectors with a gridded population-density raster for an urban district. Both sources must be brought into a common spatial reference. Output: building polygons carrying an estimated-population attribute, plus a district-level summary table.

Compare land-cover maps from two different years of the same classification scheme and produce a change layer distinguishing stable areas, gains, and losses for each class. Report the area of each change type. All outputs must share one spatial grid.

Derive an elevation profile and mean channel slope for each reach of a river-network vector using a DEM. Reaches must be ordered so upstream/downstream direction is known. Output: reaches carrying profile-derived slope values and a downstream-order identifier.

Bring three vector layers supplied in different coordinate reference systems into one projected CRS suitable for area measurement, repair any geometry that becomes invalid after transformation, and produce a short CRS report recording source and target systems per layer.

Reproject a global raster to an equal-area CRS and compute area-weighted global mean and per-continent totals of the raster values — naming the continent-boundary source you use (or explicitly declaring it as a required external input) — so that pixel counts are converted to true areas rather than naive counts.

Merge road vectors that cross two adjacent UTM zones into a single seamless layer, ensuring geometries remain valid across the zone boundary, and report the total network length in a stated linear unit.
Compute forest-cover percentage inside each protected-area polygon from a forest-cover raster, and produce a masked forest raster limited to protected areas. Both outputs must use a consistent CRS.

Identify potentially unstable slope cells: derive slope from a DEM, flag cells above a slope threshold you state explicitly that also fall inside a road-corridor buffer, and output the flagged cells as a feature layer with their slope values.

Assemble a modelling sample table by extracting, for each observation point, the values of several continuous environmental rasters plus the categorical class of a land-cover raster. Output: one table with one row per point, predictor columns per raster, and the land-cover class.

Using administrative boundaries as zones, compute total population and population density per zone from a population raster, then flag zones whose density exceeds a density threshold you state explicitly. Output: zone table with totals, densities, and a flag column.
From a multi-temporal NDVI image stack, compute per-region seasonal mean NDVI (defined by stated month ranges) and output one table where each row is a region-season pair with its mean value.
For each sub-watershed, report the share of each land-cover class and identify the dominant class; include a simple diversity measure (e.g., effective class count) per watershed.

Run a geometry quality check on an input vector layer: repair invalid geometries where possible, detect remaining overlaps between features, and flag features violating an attribute rule you state explicitly (for example, an area-below-minimum rule). Output: a cleaned layer plus a QA layer marking each issue type per feature.

Grade water samples (point locations with turbidity and chlorophyll attributes) into quality tiers defined by thresholds you state explicitly, and mark low-confidence samples — those missing either measurement — as requiring re-survey. Output: graded point layer with tier and confidence-status columns.

Compare two elevation rasters covering the same area from different sources: compute the difference surface, flag areas where the absolute difference exceeds a tolerance you state explicitly, and output a confidence raster combining difference magnitude with a slope-stability hint you state explicitly.

Apply class-dependent buffer zones around road segments — assign and declare your own radius per road class — then detect sensitive sites (a point layer) falling inside any buffer, and output matched sites annotated with the road class and buffer radius responsible.

Quantify the urban heat island: derive summer-night land-surface temperature statistics, classify urban vs rural zones from land-cover data, compute UHI intensity as the urban-rural differential, and rank administrative units by intensity. Output: ranked unit table + intensity raster.

Build a simplified flood-exposure screening: derive flow accumulation from a DEM, identify flat/sink areas, combine with a depth-proxy rule you state explicitly to screen potential inundation cells, and summarize exposed land-cover classes by area.

Assess conservation coverage: extract environmental conditions at species occurrence points, build a suitability model, identify high-suitability cells, and report how much of that high-suitability area falls inside existing protected areas versus outside.

Rank districts by solar potential: screen areas by slope and aspect suitability rules you state explicitly, exclude exclusion zones you name explicitly, overlay solar irradiance, and compute per-district potential scores for ranking.
